hypotheses.claim: Bytes moved: the cost per key follows the 64-byte lines each key brings in (1/8 for soa, 1/4 for aos16, 1 for aos64 and aos128) once the touched span leaves the cache level that held it.
predictions: equal instructions per key across layouts
at n=2097152 soa < aos16 < aos64 per key, with L1D fills per key near 1/8, 1/4 and 1
at n=2048 (aos64 128 KiB, L2-resident) a smaller gap than at n=2097152
hypotheses.falsified_if: time per key does not grow with lines per key at the DRAM-sized working set

hypotheses.claim: Instruction count or vectorization: the representations compile to different loops.
predictions: instructions per key differ between layouts; the disassembly shows different loop bodies
hypotheses.falsified_if: instructions per key are equal and the loops differ only in the stride constant

hypotheses.claim: Address span and translation: beyond lines, the span matters; aos128 touches the same lines per key as aos64 over twice the pages.
predictions: if only lines matter, aos128 costs about what aos64 costs
if span matters, aos128 is slower and has more DTLB misses per key
hypotheses.falsified_if: aos128 and aos64 cost the same per key at every size while their DTLB misses differ

hypotheses.claim: Prefetch coverage: the hardware prefetchers hide part of the DRAM latency, and how much depends on the stride.
predictions: the prefetch share of DRAM fills differs by layout
demand DRAM fills per key are larger for aos64/aos128 than for soa
hypotheses.falsified_if: prefetch and demand DRAM fills split the same way for every layout

hypotheses.claim: Frequency or host noise produces the differences.
predictions: user cycles per ns differ between variants; involuntary switches concentrate in one variant
hypotheses.falsified_if: cycle-based and time-based orderings agree and the effective cycle rate is the same for both variants

limits: Raw rows are the evidence; every value here is derived from rows.jsonl by this script.
Calling-thread user-space counts only (exclude_kernel, exclude_hv); peers count their own.
Rankings exist only for regimes whose five gates all passed.
Sign-test intervals assume independent pairs; the carry-over section shows where consecutive processes were not independent.
